title: When the Contact Turns
premise: Silas Kavanagh, a peace-delegation interpreter who has survived a decade of shifting loyalties by staying useful and invisible, receives a meeting request from his handler—dead for six months. The invitation leads him into a conspiracy inside the delegation itself: an attack engineered to look like an accident of failed diplomacy, timed to the summit's final day. As Silas races to expose it, he learns the dead handler was the architect, testing whether Silas's loyalty was to people, rules, or truth. In the end Silas chooses truth, burning his carefully built anonymity to stop the attack, and walks away from the institution that taught him to disappear—alive, but finally visible to everyone.
about_author: Z. M. Blackwood is the pen name of a former conference interpreter who spent years inside high-stakes diplomatic rooms before turning to fiction. They write thrillers about the invisible professionals who keep fragile peace processes from collapsing.

chapters.title: A Message from the Dead
chapters.summary: Silas Kavanagh's POV. During routine summit prep in Geneva, Silas receives an encrypted meeting invite from Marcus Hale, his handler who died six months ago. The message contains a phrase only Hale knew. Silas, unsettled and secretly thrilled, decides to attend rather than report it. Emotional beat: the crack in his careful invisibility—curiosity overriding ten years of discipline.

chapters.title: The Empty Chair
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. At the meeting site, Hale is absent, but a dead-drop holds a dossier: evidence that the summit's security chief, Ingrid Voss, is coordinating an 'accident' timed to the closing ceremony. Silas can't verify it—and realizes whoever sent it is watching him. Emotional beat: dread mixed with the intoxicating sense of mattering for the first time in years.

chapters.title: Rules of Interpretation
chapters.summary: Silas's POV, with a flashback to his recruitment by Hale. Silas quietly tests the dossier's claims through what he hears interpreting private delegation conversations. A delegate's offhand remark corroborates a detail. His deputy, Amara Osei, notices his distraction. Emotional beat: loyalty to the institution warring with the growing certainty that something is rotten.

chapters.title: Amara
chapters.summary: Amara Osei's POV. Amara, ambitious and sharp, has been reporting Silas's odd behavior to Voss—believing she's protecting the delegation. Through her we see Voss's charm and control, and the first hint that Amara is being groomed as a patsy. Emotional beat: her hunger to belong to power, and the reader's dramatic irony as she digs Silas's grave.

chapters.title: The Second Invitation
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Another message from 'Hale' summons him to a lakeside boathouse. There he meets a stranger claiming to be Hale's protégé, who reveals Hale's death was staged—or engineered—and that the attack will be pinned on an interpreter. Silas realizes he is both investigator and intended scapegoat. Emotional beat: the trap snapping shut; paranoia becomes survival.

chapters.title: What Voss Wants
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Voss believes the summit's peace deal will empower a regime she considers worse than war, and that a controlled catastrophe will produce a 'better' settlement. She is not a cartoon villain but a true believer. She orders surveillance on Silas and promotes Amara. Emotional beat: the seductive self-justification of power—corruption as conviction.

chapters.title: Burned
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Silas tries to warn a sympathetic delegate and is intercepted; his credentials are revoked, and Voss publicly frames him for a security breach. Hunted inside the summit perimeter, he goes to Amara, laying out the evidence. Emotional beat: betrayal, humiliation, and the raw choice between crawling back into invisibility or fighting exposed.

chapters.title: The Interpreter's Dilemma
chapters.summary: Amara's POV, torn. Amara verifies a piece of Silas's evidence herself and confronts Voss, who coolly reveals Amara was always meant to take the fall. Shaken, Amara makes contact with Silas and offers the access codes Voss gave her. Emotional beat: the theme crystallized—belonging purchased with complicity, and the cost of refusing it.

chapters.title: Closing Ceremony
chapters.summary: Alternating Silas and Amara POVs, real-time. Using Amara's access, they reach the ceremony's technical gallery as the 'accident'—a staged structural failure—is armed. Silas must interpret a hijacked announcement to buy seconds, turning his skill into a weapon. Emotional beat: white-knuckle climax; ten years of careful neutrality spent in one act of open defiance.

chapters.title: On the Record
chapters.summary: Silas's POV, weeks later. The attack is stopped; Voss is arrested, and Hale—alive, in custody—admits he used Silas as a test of conscience. Silas testifies publicly, surrendering his anonymity forever, then declines reinstatement. He and Amara part as equals. Emotional beat: quiet resolution—truth cost him everything he built, and he finally belongs to himself.
